claims.location: Format notes and 100-year TDB SPICE download
claims.finding: INPOP21a SPICE distribution includes TT-TDB in seconds with TDB argument; ordinary JPL-format files omit the time transformation.
claims.applicability: Select the TDB SPICE archive, not the ordinary planetary binary or TCB product.

claims.location: Fienga et al., 2009-06-10 author preprint, section 2.4, pp. 3-4
claims.finding: INPOP integrates the geocentric time transformation alongside dynamics, including c^-4 terms. An offset is applied before polynomial construction to satisfy the 1977 IAU origin. TT input requires an implicit mapping.
claims.applicability: Family method and normalization evidence; the older release's detailed body inventory is not asserted for INPOP21a. No extra TDB0 correction or forced J2000 zero.

claims.location: Section 2.4, p. 4, Figure 1 and following discussion
claims.finding: The reported 6.74 ns/century drift concerns INPOP08 versus offset-corrected TE405.
claims.applicability: Different models and domain; neither an INPOP21a/DE440t result nor a physical bound for this mission.

claims.location: Fienga et al., June 2021, IMCCE Notes scientifiques et techniques S110, sections 1-3
claims.finding: INPOP21a updates observations and dynamical modeling; section 3.2 compares planetary coordinates with DE440. No complete TT-TDB uncertainty bound for the selected epochs was identified in this release note.
claims.applicability: Release-specific context. Orbital discrepancies and fitted parameter uncertainties are not a clock-error certificate.

claims.location: Coordinate-time NAIF identifiers; companion multiple-access usage documentation
claims.finding: TT-TDB uses target 1000000001 relative to center 1000000000. The clock is the first returned component in seconds.
claims.applicability: Special time segment semantics; ordinary SPK distance scaling is inapplicable. CALCEPH documentation is consulted, CALCEPH is not executed.

claims.location: DE440 section 2.3 and INPOP sources above; inference recorded by this project
claims.finding: Distinct integrated ephemeris families do not guarantee independent errors: time definitions, gravitational theory, observations and numerical reader infrastructure can be shared.
claims.applicability: Differences diagnose disagreement. Even exact agreement cannot bound common error; no covariance, probabilistic independence or physical certificate is inferred.
